question: How many members sit on the Maryland Real Estate Commission?
explanation: Section 17-202 sets the Commission at 9 members appointed by the Governor: 5 licensees and 4 consumer members. Five is only the number of professional members.

question: A Maryland Guaranty Fund claim must reach the Commission within what time after the loss is discovered?
optionA: 3 years
optionB: 1 year
optionC: 6 months
optionD: 5 years
explanation: Section 17-404(d) requires a claim within 3 years after the claimant discovers, or with ordinary diligence should have discovered, the loss. One year is the time to apply for a license after passing the exam, not a claim deadline.

question: The Maryland Commission may summarily suspend a license, with a hearing afterward, when the licensee:
optionA: Misses a required continuing education course
optionB: Fails to account promptly for trust money
optionC: Advertises with an unapproved nickname
optionD: Moves to a new branch office without notice
explanation: Section 17-328 lets the Commission suspend summarily, with prompt notice and a hearing after, for failing to account promptly for trust money, refusing to show trust records, or a felony conviction. The other lapses go through the ordinary hearing process under 17-324.

question: Each Maryland real estate hearing board must include at least:
optionA: Two licensees and one outside attorney
optionB: Three consumer members and no licensees
optionC: One administrative judge and two brokers
optionD: One professional and one consumer member
explanation: Under 17-325 a hearing board has at least 3 Commission members, at least one professional member and at least one consumer member. Its decision is treated as the Commission's final decision under 17-326(d).

question: Maryland's salesperson prelicensing course must include an approved real estate ethics course of how many clock hours?
explanation: Section 17-303(d) requires a basic course of no more than 60 clock hours that includes a 3 clock hour ethics course. Fifteen hours is the continuing education total for each renewal term.

question: How many clock hours of continuing education must a Maryland licensee complete in each 2-year license term?
explanation: Section 17-315(a) requires at least 15 clock hours of continuing education during the preceding 2-year term, including set courses on legal updates, fair housing, ethics and brokerage relationships.

question: Unless reactivated, a Maryland license placed on inactive status expires after:
optionA: 18 months
optionB: 2 years
optionC: 4 years
optionD: 3 years
explanation: Section 17-316(c) makes an inactive license expire 3 years after it was placed on inactive status unless it is reactivated. After that the person must qualify for a license again under 17-301 to 17-308.

question: To renew a Maryland license, continuing education must be completed no later than:
optionA: 60 days before the license expires
optionB: On the license expiration date
optionC: 30 days before the license expires
optionD: 90 days after the license expires
explanation: Section 17-314(c)(1)(iv) requires the continuing education to be done not later than 30 days before expiration; missing it brings a reinstatement fee. Sixty days is when the Commission sends the renewal notice, not the deadline.

question: A Maryland seller's agent must give an unrepresented buyer the written agency disclosure no later than:
optionA: First scheduled face-to-face contact
optionB: Signing of the buyer's purchase contract
optionC: First telephone call or email exchange
optionD: Third business day after the first showing
explanation: Section 17-530(b) requires the written disclosure by the first scheduled face-to-face contact. If first contact is by phone or email, the agent must also say then, through that medium, whom the agent represents.

question: Under Maryland law, who may act as a dual agent in a residential transaction?
optionA: Any salesperson with written consent from both parties
optionB: Only the broker or a designated branch office manager
optionC: Only the listing salesperson on the property
optionD: Any associate broker affiliated with the firm
explanation: Sections 17-528(j) and 17-530.1(b) allow only the licensed broker, or a branch office manager the broker designates, to be the dual agent, and only with the written informed consent of all parties. Salespersons and associate brokers serve as intra-company agents instead.

question: In a Maryland dual agency, the broker assigns each party:
optionA: Subagent from a cooperating firm
optionB: Single transaction broker for both sides
optionC: Separate intra-company agent from the firm
optionD: Buyer's agent from another brokerage
explanation: Under 17-530.1(b)(1)(ii) the dual agent assigns one affiliated licensee as intra-company agent for the seller and another for the buyer. A dual agent may not also act as an intra-company agent in the same transaction.

question: A Maryland brokerage agreement with a seller must include:
optionA: Automatic renewal unless the client cancels in writing
optionB: End date that takes effect only after 30 days' notice
optionC: Promise that the broker will produce a buyer at full price
optionD: Definite end date that needs no notice from the client
explanation: Section 17-534(b) requires a definite termination date effective automatically without notice from the client, plus the compensation, cooperation terms and a cancellation provision. Accepting a listing without one is also a ground for discipline under 17-322(b)(10).

question: Which of these is confidential information under Maryland's brokerage relationship law?
optionA: Seller's willingness to accept a lower price
optionB: Known leak in the basement foundation wall
optionC: Property's current zoning classification
optionD: Age and condition of the furnace
explanation: Section 17-528(h) defines confidential information to include a seller's willingness to take less, a party's motivation and negotiating strategy, and 17-532(b)(2) bars disclosing it without written consent. A known leak is a material fact that must be disclosed.

question: After a Maryland brokerage relationship ends, the licensee must still:
optionA: Present every later offer to the former client in writing
optionB: Keep the client's financial information confidential
optionC: Keep marketing the property for 30 days
optionD: Advise the former client on pricing for a year
explanation: Section 17-534(d) ends the licensee's duties when the relationship ends except accounting for trust money and keeping the client's personal and financial information confidential, unless the client consents in writing or it becomes public from another source.

question: A Maryland buyer who got no disclosure or disclaimer statement before contracting may rescind within how long after receiving it?
optionA: 3 days
optionB: 10 days
optionC: 5 days
optionD: 7 days
explanation: Real Property 10-702(h) gives the buyer an unconditional right to rescind before receiving the statement or within 5 days after receiving it, with the deposit returned. A buyer who received it before contracting has no such right.

question: A Maryland broker must deposit trust money into the trust account within:
optionA: 3 business days after the money is received
optionB: 10 days after the contract is signed by the buyer
optionC: 24 hours after the earnest money check clears the bank
optionD: 7 business days after the contract is accepted
explanation: Section 17-502(b) requires the broker to deposit trust money promptly, but not more than 7 business days after acceptance of the contract by both parties, unless the parties direct otherwise in writing. A salesperson must hand it to the broker promptly.

question: Maryland licensees must keep transaction records for how long after a closed transaction's closing date?
optionA: 5 years
optionB: 3 years
optionC: 7 years
optionD: 2 years
explanation: Section 17-507(b)(2) requires records to be kept for 5 years from closing, or 5 years from the listing date if the deal never closed; property management records run 5 years after the management agreement ends.

question: A Maryland broker must hold trust money in a financial institution that is:
optionA: Chosen by the buyer anywhere in the country
optionB: Located in Maryland with insured deposits
optionC: Located in the broker's home state, insured or not
optionD: Named by the seller in the listing agreement
explanation: Section 17-503 requires trust money to be deposited in a financial institution located in Maryland whose deposits are insured, such as by the FDIC or the NCUA, except as 17-505 allows by written instruction.

question: Before giving a client a home improvement contractor's name, a Maryland licensee must:
optionA: Confirm the contractor carries a written guarantee
optionB: Refer only contractors the broker has used
optionC: Verify its license yearly and tell the client where to check
optionD: Collect a referral agreement signed by the client and the contractor
explanation: Section 17-527.4(c) requires annual verification that a home improvement contractor holds a Home Improvement Commission license and telling the client the website and the date checked. Licensees need not verify other service providers such as lenders or inspectors.

question: Maryland's supervision regulation treats regular training sessions as a factor if held at least:
optionA: Once every 2 months
optionB: Once every 6 months
optionC: Once a year
optionD: Once a week
explanation: COMAR 09.11.05.03B lists training or education sessions held regularly at least once every 2 months as a factor in reasonable and adequate supervision. If supervision is challenged, the broker bears the burden of proving it was adequate.

question: A Maryland salesperson's advertisement must meaningfully and conspicuously include:
optionA: Salesperson's license number and expiration date
optionB: Business logo in place of its written name
optionC: Salesperson's home address and personal phone number
optionD: Full name of the affiliated business, not a logo
explanation: Section 17-527.2(b) requires the licensee's name or approved designated name and the full name of the affiliated business, not a logo. COMAR 09.11.02.01G also requires the broker's or branch manager's phone number if an individual number is used.

question: Maryland law bars which word or phrase from a team's name?
optionA: Group
optionB: Real estate
optionC: Team
optionD: And associates
explanation: Section 17-547(a) bars team names with "real estate", "real estate brokerage" or any term suggesting services independent of the broker. Section 17-543 contemplates teams using names like team, group or "and associates".

question: Unless the brokerage agreement says otherwise, a Maryland listing agent must present written offers that arrive:
optionA: Even if the property is already under contract
optionB: Only until a contract is signed by both parties
optionC: Only if they beat the current contract price
optionD: Only after the supervising broker reviews and approves them
explanation: Section 17-532(b)(1)(ii) requires timely presentation of all written offers and counteroffers even if the property is under contract, unless the brokerage agreement says otherwise. COMAR 09.11.02.02H requires them presented in full.

question: A Maryland salesperson may accept a commission for brokerage services only from:
optionA: Seller who signed the listing agreement
optionB: Buyer who received the brokerage services
optionC: Broker with whom the salesperson is affiliated
optionD: Cooperating broker in the deal
explanation: Under 17-310 and 17-322(b)(21) a salesperson works only on behalf of the affiliated broker and may take compensation only from that broker. A title insurance producer may pay a salesperson at settlement only under the broker's written disbursement authorization (17-604(c)).

question: A Maryland licensee convicted of a felony must disclose it to the Commission within:
optionA: 30 days after conviction or release
optionB: 60 days after the final appeal
optionC: 5 business days after the arrest
optionD: 10 days after conviction or release
explanation: Section 17-328(a)(4) allows summary suspension of a licensee who does not disclose a felony conviction within 10 days after the conviction or release from incarceration, whichever is later. Thirty days is the time to answer a written Commission inquiry under COMAR 09.11.01.13.

question: Under Maryland's Code of Ethics, a for-sale sign may be placed on a property only with:
optionA: Listing broker's verbal approval
optionB: Owner's prior consent
optionC: Neighbors' written permission
optionD: County zoning office approval
explanation: COMAR 09.11.02.03C bars signs giving notice of property for sale, rent, lease or exchange without the owner's prior consent. COMAR 09.11.02.02G likewise bars advertising property without authority.

question: A Maryland licensee buying a home for personal use must disclose the licensing status in writing:
optionA: Before the first showing of the home
optionB: Within 10 days after contract acceptance
optionC: No later than when an offer is submitted
optionD: At the settlement table
explanation: COMAR 09.11.02.02D requires a licensee acquiring an interest in real property, or acting for immediate family or an owned entity, to disclose licensing status in writing no later than the time an offer is submitted.

question: Maryland requires a competitive market analysis to state conspicuously on its first page that it:
optionA: Is not an appraisal
optionB: Guarantees the list price
optionC: Was reviewed by an appraiser
optionD: Expires after 90 days
explanation: COMAR 09.11.02.02F requires the Competitive Market Analysis Disclosure on the first page saying the analysis is not an appraisal. Any comparable in which the licensee has an interest must also be disclosed.

question: A Maryland licensee may accept compensation from more than one party to a transaction only with:
optionA: Approval of the supervising broker alone
optionB: Prior written approval of the Commission
optionC: Consent of the paying party alone
optionD: Full knowledge of all the parties
explanation: COMAR 09.11.02.02C bars accepting compensation from more than one party without the full knowledge of all the parties. A broker's approval alone does not satisfy the rule.

question: To influence sales, a Maryland licensee may advertise free appraisals only if:
optionA: Offered only to sellers who list with the firm
optionB: Free to anyone who asks, for any purpose
optionC: Limited to homes in the licensee's farm area
optionD: Done by a licensed appraiser the broker pays
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(9) makes it a ground for discipline to solicit by prizes, free lots, lotteries or contests, or by advertising free appraisals unless the advertiser will appraise free of charge for any person regardless of purpose.
